title: The Ship of Theseus
summary: Plutarch tells how the Athenians preserved the ship of the hero Theseus by replacing its planks as they decayed, until it became a standing example for philosophers: was it still the same ship? Thomas Hobbes sharpened the puzzle. If someone kept every discarded plank and rebuilt them into a ship, which of the two would be the ship of Theseus? The case is still a centrepiece of debates about identity over time and about how an object relates to what it is made of.
citations: Thomas Hobbes, De Corpore (Elements of Philosophy, Concerning Body), Part II, ch. 11 (1655)

essay.creator: Daniel Bonevac
